question.prompt: Which of the following integers cannot be written as the sum of four consecutive odd integers?

solutions.explanation:
Four consecutive odd integers are equally spaced. Their mean is the integer halfway between the middle two terms, because the outer two terms have that same midpoint. Between two consecutive odd integers lies an even integer, so this mean is even.

The sum is therefore four times an even integer, which must be a multiple of \(8\). But
\[
100=8\cdot12+4,
\]
so \(100\) cannot be such a sum.

To check that every other choice is possible, we can exhibit the required sums:
\[
\begin{aligned}
16&=1+3+5+7,\\
40&=7+9+11+13,\\
72&=15+17+19+21,\\
200&=47+49+51+53.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the integer that cannot be written in the required way is \(\boxed{100}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Use the average of the four integers
